comparison: Perfect agreement on the main conclusion (C71, C72). Both strongly support the hierarchical suppression model as the central finding. OpenEval cites convergence of multiple experimental results; peer reviewers call it 'strong evidence' and 'of wide interest.'

Strong agreement on Split GAL4 characterization (C45-C58). Both support the anatomical and functional characterization. OpenEval emphasizes methodological soundness; peer reviewers note the work is 'carefully done' and tools 'will be very useful for fly workers.'

Agreement on eye bristle mechanosensory neuron identification and function (C40-C44). Both support these claims. OpenEval cites anatomical and optogenetic evidence; peer reviewers accept the characterization with no concerns raised.

Significant disagreement on hierarchical suppression demonstration with defined sensory populations (C65-C70). OpenEval finds claims supported by Figure 5 data; all three peer reviewers raised concerns about eye-wing grooming interactions, noting eye grooming appears limited and requesting additional experiments to balance stimulation.

Agreement on anatomical characterization (C19-C21). OpenEval supports based on confocal microscopy; peer result R1 also covers behavioral claims C22-C25 and accepts both anatomical and behavioral findings with no concerns.

Agreement on optogenetic behavioral responses (C22-C25). OpenEval supports based on Figure 1H and videos; peer reviewers accepted the characterization and use of GAL4 lines for optogenetic activation.

Agreement on core experimental finding of temporal sequence and persistence (C26, C27, C31-C33). OpenEval finds strong evidence for persistent neural activity; peer reviewers endorse 'persistent state of activation' and call it 'strong evidence for the hierarchical suppression model.'

Agreement on decapitation control experiment (C28-C30). OpenEval supports the hierarchical suppression model over delay mechanism; peer result R2 covers broader claims but strongly endorses hierarchical suppression findings.
Agreement on active suppression demonstration (C34-C37). OpenEval supports based on reactivation data; peer result R2 covers these claims within broader support for hierarchical suppression model.

Partial overlap on sensory pathway controls (C61-C64). OpenEval supports specificity and differential persistence; peer result R5 includes these claims but focuses concerns on the interaction experiments (C65-C70) rather than the individual pathway controls.

Agreement on persistence phenomenon (C101-C105). OpenEval supports based on current and prior work; peer reviewers explicitly endorsed this finding as 'long-lasting bout of grooming' that 'should lead to interesting extensions.'

Agreement on persistent traces and mechanism (C108-C113). OpenEval supports the inference of persistent traces from continued grooming; peer result R8 endorses the persistence finding broadly, though focuses on the empirical observation rather than mechanistic details.

Disagreement on interpretation of eye grooming duration (C86-C92). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting observation is clear but interpretation speculative; peer reviewers also uncertain, with Reviewer 1 stating 'not totally convinced' and suggesting possible inhibition of eye grooming by body grooming.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding unexplained observations (C93-C99). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting multiple speculative mechanisms; peer result R7 questions the interpretation and requests explanation, indicating current explanation insufficient.

Minimal overlap on model revision (C118-C122). OpenEval supports the distinction between previous and new model scope; peer result R8 touches on C122 within broader endorsement of persistence findings.

OpenEval supports theoretical framework from prior literature (C1, C2, C8, C9, C10). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these background claims were not specifically addressed in peer reviews.
OpenEval supports prior findings from Seeds et al., 2014 (C11-C15). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these background claims.
OpenEval supports claims about mechanosensory neurons and optogenetic evidence (C73-C75). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these claims were not separately addressed by peer reviewers.

OpenEval rates bristle number analysis as uncertain (C78-C81), noting inconclusive interpretation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not address this mechanistic speculation.

OpenEval supports methodological decisions about optogenetic tools (C129-C132). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these methodological justifications.
